quote: $50–$300 of home-center materials ... $50–$300 materials only ... against $50–$300 for DIY materials.
issue: The recurring DIY cost figure '$50–$300 (materials only / home-center materials / DIY materials)' traces to NO pack as a DIY repair-materials total. The only '$50–$300' figures in any research file are HomeGuide's 'Replace individual broken slate $50–$300 / tile' (facts-materials-economics.md line 132) and 'Replace individual tiles $50–$300 / tile' (line 264) — a per-tile slate/clay/concrete UNIT cost, not a general DIY home-center materials budget (sealant, a shingle bundle, fasteners). The GOVERNS pack (GAP-service-decisions §1/§2/§4) lists NO DIY-materials figure at all. The draft's own KEY SOURCED FIGURES line (diy-vs-professional-roof-repair.md line 73) bundles 'DIY materials $50–$300' with no named source, and the GAPS note (line 86) presents it as the de-fab replacement for the dropped '$250–$400' without ever sourcing the $50–$300 itself. Compounding it: comparisonRows[0] labels the row 'Out-of-pocket cost (Angi)' with itemA '$50–$300 materials only', and faqs[3] reads '$360–$1,550, per Angi, against $50–$300 for DIY materials' — both pin the unsourced figure beside an Angi attribution, falsely implying Angi sourced the $50–$300. Repeated 6+ times as the DIY side's headline cost.
fix: De-quantify the DIY side to qualitative home-center-materials framing wherever the bare '$50–$300' now stands, removing the implied source. (verdict.alternateScenario) '...costs $50–$300 in materials...' → '...costs only home-center materials...'. (residentialSection.content[0]) '...stays inside the homeowner's $50–$300 material budget...' → '...stays inside the homeowner's home-center material budget...'. (faqs[3].answer) '$360–$1,550, per Angi, against $50–$300 for DIY materials.' → '$360–$1,550, per Angi; DIY materials run far less — sealant, a shingle bundle, and fasteners from a home center.' Keep the real Angi $360–$1,550 and the $45–$75/hr labor (both sourced). ALTERNATIVELY (b) replace with a figure that actually traces to a pack — Modernize/Angi 'Replace a few / patch shingles $150–$400' (facts-materials-economics line 101) attributed in-text — but option (a) de-quantification is cleaner since no pack figure is a true DIY-materials-only total.

quote: **DIY roof repair** on a two-story Essex County colonial reaches the 6-to-30-foot height band that the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics ties to 64.4% of fatal construction falls, the point at which a harnessed crew replaces the homeowner on the roof.
issue: The BLS 64.4% (6–30 ft) figure is WORKER/occupational fatality data. GAP-service-decisions §0 (line 17) is explicit: BLS CFOI 2023 data 'may be used ONLY as a clearly-labeled "even among trained professionals…" contrast — never applied to homeowners.' Here the 64.4% worker statistic is attached directly to a DIY homeowner's height exposure with no worker-contrast label — the exact application the GOVERNS pack forbids. detailedAnalysis[0].content[1] (line 487) does this correctly ('even among trained, harnessed construction workers, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics recorded 421 fatal falls... and 64.4% of fatal construction falls came from 6 to 30 feet'), so the page already carries the labeled version; this second use in residentialSection drops the label. The figure and the 6–30 ft band are real and traceable (GAP §1 line 37); only the unlabeled application to the homeowner is the defect.
fix: Relabel, do not delete the fact. Rewrite to keep the height band as the homeowner-relevant point while marking the 64.4% as worker data: '**DIY roof repair** on a two-story Essex County colonial puts the homeowner in the 6-to-30-foot height band — the band that, even among trained construction workers, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics ties to 64.4% of fatal construction falls — the point at which a harnessed crew replaces the homeowner on the roof.'
refuteReason: Survives. GAP-service-decisions.md §0 line 17 (a CRITICAL CORRECTION in the GOVERNS pack) mandates the BLS CFOI figure be 'used ONLY as a clearly-labeled "even among trained professionals…" contrast — never applied to homeowners,' reinforced at §4 line 102 ('LABELED as worker/occupational data only'). residentialSection.content[2] (service-vs-service.ts line 521) attaches the 64.4% directly to the DIY homeowner with no such label, while the correct labeled form already exists at detailedAnalysis[0].content[1] (line 487) — proving the omission is a slip, not a constraint, and is fixable by relabel without losing the fact.
